| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `latet version` | Print the Latet version. |
| `latet serve` | Run the gateway in the foreground. |
| `latet start` | Start the background daemon (no-op when it is already running). |
| `latet stop` | Stop the background daemon. |
| `latet status` | Show whether the local daemon runs, or the connected server accepts this computer's token. |
| `latet env` | Print the environment variables that route a client through Latet. |
| `latet dashboard` | Open the dashboard here or on the connected server: what reached the model, and how it was masked. |

| `latet copilot` | Run GitHub Copilot CLI through Latet, for this session only (a provider of your own); arguments pass through. |
| `latet run` | Run a script or tool with OPENAI_BASE_URL, ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL and GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL pointing at Latet. |
| `latet reload` | Apply the configuration file to the running daemon, without a restart. |
| `latet doctor` | Check the daemon, the plugin bridge, masking and the agent integrations. |
| `latet global-uninstall` | Take Latet out of your agents for good: what `latet global-install` did, undone. |
| `latet upgrade` | Install the latest release of Latet from GitHub, with local name detection and the text in images. |

| `latet backup` | Save your installation in one file, encrypted with a passphrase: to move it to another machine. |
| `latet restore` | Restore a backup here: your settings, and the vault with its key when it holds them. |
| `latet connect` | Connect this computer to a Latet server: your agents' requests are masked there, in your own space. |

| `latet tutorial` | See Latet at work in your browser, on a sandbox of its own with invented data. |

| `latet identity set` | Tell Latet whose identity to mask (in the container it cannot see it), then apply it. |

| `latet llm trust` | Trust the certificate of the reviewer's server on another machine of yours (self-signed). |

| `latet project on` | Turn Latet on again in a project. |
| `latet repositories` | The repositories Latet remembers, each with its state; forget one that stays unreadable. |
| `latet repositories forget` | Take a repository out of the list, the daemon's memory too: no change is weighed in it until a conversation reaches it again. It lowers protection: run it yourself, in a terminal of your own. |

| `latet rules remove` | Remove a recognizer from config.yaml (or one project's settings), then apply the change. |
| `latet rules suggest` | Find code-like values that no rule covers, grouped by shape (AA-999999), on this machine. |
| `latet rules export` | Write your rules to a file, for a colleague: terms, recognizers, policies and the rest. |
| `latet rules import` | Add a colleague's rules to yours: what adds protection applies at once. |

| `latet config add` | Add an item to a list of config.yaml (`terms`, `pii`, `allow_values`...) and apply it. |
| `latet config remove` | Take an item out of a list of config.yaml and apply it (taking protection away waits for the user). |

| `latet server init` | Prepare a Latet server: its master key, the database's tables, and the first administration token. |
| `latet server migrate` | Bring the database's tables to this version of Latet (one machine at a time: the others wait for it). |
| `latet server run` | Run an instance of the Latet server in the foreground: the container's command, and the services'. |
| `latet server ready` | Whether this machine's instance answers ready (PostgreSQL and Valkey answer it): exit 0, else 1. |
| `latet server certificate` | Show a certificate's fingerprint and expiry, or make a self-signed one for a first try. |
| `latet server status` | The server's status, vault limits, log chain and edition checks. |
| `latet server service install` | Show and install a systemd unit or a Windows service for the machine's Latet. |
| `latet server people add` | Add a person and show their one-time code, to be given to them alone. |
| `latet server people list` | Everyone: enabled or not, computers connected, last seen and tampered token rows. |
| `latet server people disable` | Disable a person: every token of theirs stops on every instance within seconds; their space is kept. |
| `latet server people enable` | Enable a person again: their tokens and their space work again. |
| `latet server people remove` | Remove a person: their tokens stop, and their space (vault, history, settings) is deleted, once you agree. |
| `latet server people code` | A new one-time code: whoever uses it can connect as this person and open their dashboard; recorded. |
| `latet server people tokens` | A person's computers; `--revoke` or `--revoke-all` stops their tokens. |
| `latet server keys add` | Make an API key, shown once or written privately with `--out`. |
| `latet server keys list` | Every API key: enabled or not, when it was last used, and its vault limit if it has one of its own. |
| `latet server keys tokens` | An API key's tokens: each one's name, what it may do, whether it serves the key's agents (has an address), and when it was last used; `--revoke` stops one. |
| `latet server keys add-token` | Give an API key another token with the permissions you choose, shown once or written privately with `--out`. |
| `latet server keys rotate` | Rotate one of an API key's tokens: its old secret and addresses stop on every instance within seconds. |
| `latet server keys limit` | Set how many values an API key's vault may hold, or give it the server's limit again. |
| `latet server keys forget` | Forget values of an API key's vault: each taken out of it on every instance within seconds, once you agree. |
| `latet server keys disable` | Disable an API key: its addresses stop on every instance within seconds; its space is kept. |
| `latet server keys enable` | Enable an API key again. |
| `latet server keys remove` | Remove an API key: it stops, and its space is deleted, once you agree. |
| `latet server config` | The settings the server shares: destinations, the reviewer, text recognition, history, retention (`--key`: an API key's own settings and rules, the keys of `latet config`). |
| `latet server config get` | Print a shared setting (or every one). |
| `latet server config set` | Change a shared setting: every space applies it at once. |
| `latet server config reset` | Replace an unreadable shared settings row with defaults; never reset settings that open. |
| `latet server config add` | Add an item to a list of the shared settings (`--key`: of an API key's): every space has it at once. |
| `latet server config remove` | Take an item out of a list of the shared settings (`--key`: of an API key's). |
| `latet server rules` | An API key's own recognizers and rules (`--key`). Rules for everyone are planned for the Enterprise Edition. |
| `latet server rules add` | Add an API key's recognizers (or update those with the same name), checked here first as `latet rules test` does. Their examples are not checked against a vault: invent them. |
| `latet server rules list` | An API key's recognizers, and whether each one loads. |
| `latet server rules remove` | Remove an API key's recognizer. |
| `latet server rules import` | Add a rules file to an API key's settings: what adds protection; with `--all`, what lowers it too. |
| `latet server rules export` | Write an API key's rules to a file (`--key`; the terms are values in clear), to share them by hand (`latet rules import`, or Import in the dashboard). |
| `latet server admin-token issue` | Issue an administration token once; `--out` keeps its secret out of a script's log. |
| `latet server admin-token list` | Every token: this marks the one in use; tampered rows open nothing; never a secret. |
| `latet server admin-token revoke` | Revoke a token; revoking this or the last one asks and explains the way back. |
| `latet server log` | The administration log: who did what, when, on what, from where (never a value); `verify` checks its chain. |
| `latet server log verify` | Walk the log's chain and print its head for a copy kept elsewhere. |

## `latet version`

Print the Latet version.

## `latet serve`

Run the gateway in the foreground.

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--port` `INT` |  | Local port to listen on (127.0.0.1 only). |
| `--capture` `PATH` |  | Write raw exchanges (credentials redacted) to this local directory. |
| `--log-level` `TEXT` | `info` | uvicorn log level. |
| `--passthrough`, `--no-passthrough` | off | Forward without masking (debugging only). |
| `--host` `TEXT` |  | The address to listen on: 127.0.0.1, or 0.0.0.0 in the container image. |

| --- | --- | --- |

## `latet dashboard`

Open the dashboard here or on the connected server: what reached the model, and how it was masked.

On a computer connected to a server an agent cannot run it: the sign-in link opens every original masked for you
and your settings, from wherever the server is reached.

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--print-url` | off | Print the login link instead of opening it. |

## `latet run`

Run a script or tool with OPENAI_BASE_URL, ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL and GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL pointing at Latet.

For programs that read those variables, such as the OpenAI, Anthropic and Google GenAI SDKs: their
requests go through Latet. Any other program runs as usual. `latet run claude`, `codex`, `opencode`,
`gemini` or `copilot` is `latet claude`, `latet codex`, `latet opencode`, `latet gemini` or `latet copilot`.

Every other argument is passed to the command as is.

## `latet reload`

Apply the configuration file to the running daemon, without a restart.

## `latet doctor`

Check the daemon, the plugin bridge, masking and the agent integrations.

## `latet global-uninstall`

Take Latet out of your agents for good: what `latet global-install` did, undone.

Every agent's settings go back as they were, byte for byte; Latet no longer starts at login;
the daemon stops. Your rules stay in config.yaml, for `latet claude` and the others.

## `latet upgrade`

Install the latest release of Latet from GitHub, with local name detection and the text in images.

First it copies what a new version may migrate, your vault, history and settings, into a folder of Latet's
data folder (`backups/before-<version>-<time>`; the three newest copies are kept): a copy that cannot be
made stops the upgrade with nothing changed. Then it stops the daemon and starts it again after. On Windows,
which replaces no file of a program that runs, it installs the release in a window of its own once the
command has ended. Where name detection and the text in images cannot be installed, a Latet that has
neither is installed without them; one that has them is left as it was.

With `--to` it installs that release instead; an older one only when you run it yourself, never an agent.
Going back to a version a copy was taken under, it offers to put that copy back, and says how many values
the vault has learnt since, which would be lost. At the version installed it takes no copy.

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--to` `TEXT` |  | Install this release (0.9.9) instead of the latest. |

## `latet global-install`

Route your agents through Latet for good: every session, in the terminal and in the IDE.

It shows everything it would change, then asks once: the agents it routes (their settings backed
up first), Latet started at login, the profile and the countries, what is masked as your
identity, Claude Code's auto mode reviewer, and the port. `latet global-uninstall` takes it all
away. The options choose otherwise than the defaults, such as `--agents claude --no-autostart`.
Run by an agent or a script, it needs `--yes`, once the user agreed: without a terminal of yours it
changes nothing.

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--yes`, `-y` | off | Apply it without asking (an agent or a script, once the user agreed). |
| `--profile` `TEXT` |  | balanced, max or secrets. |
| `--identity`, `--no-identity` | asks | Mask this machine's user names, host name and git author. |
| `--agents` `TEXT` |  | The agents to route: claude, codex, opencode (comma-separated), or none. Not given: every installed one. |
| `--ner`, `--no-ner` | asks | Download the local name and address model (needs the ner extra). |
| `--ocr`, `--no-ocr` | asks | Download the text recognition models for images (needs the ocr extra). |
| `--auto-mode-review` `TEXT` |  | Claude Code's auto mode reviewer: block, allow-identity, or the details to let through (user_name, paths, host_name, git_author; user_name=surrogate gives it a fake user name). |
| `--autostart`, `--no-autostart` | asks | Start Latet when you log in (default: yes). |
| `--dashboard`, `--no-dashboard` | asks | Open the dashboard at the end. |
| `--port` `TEXT` |  | The daemon's port, or auto: keep it, or move to a free one if it cannot be used. |
| `--id-regions` `TEXT` |  | Countries whose ID and tax numbers to recognise, comma-separated (such as IT,DE,US); the default adds this machine's country. |

## `latet backup`

Save your installation in one file, encrypted with a passphrase: to move it to another machine.

In it: your settings (config.yaml) and the local reviewer's trusted certificates. With `--vault`,
the vault and its root key too: the other machine then makes the same fakes, remembers the values
found so far, and keeps restoring conversations started here. With `--history`, the dashboard's
history. Never the reviewer's API key, the bridge token or your agents' settings: each machine
has its own. Restore it with `latet restore FILE`; without the passphrase nobody can read it,
you included. The passphrase is asked twice, or read from standard input.

| Argument | | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `FILE` | required | Where to write it, such as latet-backup.latet. |

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--vault` | off | Also the vault and its root key: the same fakes there, and conversations still restored. |
| `--history` | off | Also the dashboard's history (needs `--vault`). |

## `latet restore`

Restore a backup here: your settings, and the vault with its key when it holds them.

It reads and checks the whole file first, shows what it holds and what in its settings lowers
protection compared with yours, and asks you. Kept from this machine: its port, its identity
(added to the backup's), and nothing of capture_dir or api_key_file. With a vault, the daemon
is stopped and started again around it; this machine's own vault and key, if it has values, are
replaced only with `--replace`, after saving them in a backup of their own with the same
passphrase. What it moves aside stays in a dated folder next to the vault.

| Argument | | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `FILE` | optional | A file of `latet backup`. |

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--replace` | off | Replace this machine's own vault and key (saved first, same passphrase). |
| `--paths` `TEXT` |  | OLD=NEW: project folders under OLD are under NEW here (repeat it). |
| `--abort` | off | Undo a restore that was cut off. |

## `latet connect`

Connect this computer to a Latet server: your agents' requests are masked there, in your own space.

It shows what changes and asks first, at your own terminal; an agent cannot run it. The code an administrator gave
you works once, within 24 hours: it is asked for, hidden, or read from standard input with `--code -`. This
computer gets a personal token, which your agents use, and a computer key, which only Latet's own commands use for
your dashboard and identity, both kept in its credential store (or a private file); the server gets this
computer's identity (user name, host name, git author) to mask it. From then on `latet claude`, `latet codex`,
`latet opencode`, `latet run` and what `latet agents apply` set up go to the server, and your settings are there,
in your dashboard (`latet dashboard`). `latet disconnect` undoes it.

| Argument | | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `URL` | required | The server's address, such as https://latet.acme.lan. |

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--fingerprint` `TEXT` |  | The fingerprint of the server's self-signed certificate (sha256:… or AB:CD:…), as your administrator read it on the server's machine. |
| `--code` `TEXT` |  | The one-time code an administrator gave you: `--code -` reads it from standard input; not given, it is asked for, hidden. Written here, other users of this computer can read it while the command runs. |
| `--yes`, `-y` | off | Connect without asking, where no terminal is there (a script of yours). |

## `latet disconnect`

Disconnect this computer from its Latet server: its token is revoked and forgotten, and your agents come back to
the Latet of this computer.

It shows what changes back and asks first, at your own terminal; an agent cannot run it. A server that does not
answer is forgotten here all the same, and it says how an administrator revokes this computer's token there. It
leaves no copy of the token or of your space's address in what Latet wrote: a file it cannot clean is named, and
the computer stays connected until it can, so that it can be run again.

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--yes`, `-y` | off | Disconnect without asking, where no terminal is there (a script of yours). |

## `latet tutorial`

See Latet at work in your browser, on a sandbox of its own with invented data.

A pretend agent talks to a pretend model through the real Latet, and the dashboard shows what it did, chapter
by chapter. Nothing leaves your computer. Your own settings, vault and history are never touched: the sandbox is
a temporary folder on a port of its own, deleted when you press Ctrl+C or end it in the page. The one file
written outside it is `tutorial.json` in your data folder: the ids of the chapters you finished.

| Argument | | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CHAPTER` | optional | The chapter to open first, such as basics (`--list` shows them). |

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--keep` | off | Keep the sandbox's folder when it ends, and say where it is. |
| `--list` | off | Print the chapters and which you finished, then stop. |
| `--print-url` | off | Print the sign-in link instead of opening it in the browser. |

## `latet llm status`

Show the reviewer's settings and whether its server answers (with the sample text).

## `latet llm prompt`

Print what the reviewer is told: Latet's own instructions, then your guidance, if any.

Latet's part is fixed, the text its benchmark measures. Yours follows it: `llm_review.guidance`,
then a project's own `review_guidance` (see `latet llm guidance`).

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--project` `PATH` |  | For the project in this folder (your own settings for it). |

## `latet llm guidance`

Show or set your guidance to the local reviewer, added after Latet's own instructions.

Say what else is confidential in your work, or what to leave alone: "Ward and department names
are confidential", "PRJ- followed by digits is an internal project". It applies to the texts
reviewed from then on, and is sent to the reviewer's server with each review: describe kinds of
values, and keep the confidential values themselves in `terms`. With `--project`, it is for that
project only, after the global one. Changed by an agent, it waits for the user's approval.

| Argument | | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TEXT` | optional | The new guidance (`-`: standard input). None: print the one set. |

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--file` `PATH` |  | Read the new guidance from this file. |
| `--clear` | off | Remove it. |
| `--project` `PATH` |  | For the project in this folder (your own settings for it). |
| `--wait` | off | When the change waits for the user's approval, wait for the answer. |

## `latet llm key`

Save the API key of the reviewer's server, or forget it (`--remove`).

The key is asked without showing it, or read from standard input, and kept in the operating
system's credential store, never in config.yaml. A key in the variable `api_key_env` names, or in
`api_key_file`, comes first. The running daemon uses the new key at once.

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--remove` | off | Forget the saved key. |

## `latet llm trust`

Trust the certificate of the reviewer's server on another machine of yours (self-signed).

It shows the certificate's SHA-256 fingerprint: compare it with the one on the server, for example
`openssl x509 -noout -fingerprint -sha256 -in cert.pem` there. Once trusted, only that certificate
is accepted, checked before any text is sent.

| Argument | | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `URL` | optional | The server's https:// address (default: llm_review.url). |

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--fingerprint` `TEXT` |  | The fingerprint you expect (sha256:...): trusted without asking when it matches. |
| `--remove` | off | Trust no certificate of its own any more. |

## `latet llm test`

Review a text as Latet would before sending it: what the reviewer finds beyond the detectors.

It runs on this machine only, and prints categories and where they are (line:column), never the
values themselves. With `--project`, with that project's rules and guidance.

| Argument | | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `FILE` | optional | The text to review (`-`: standard input). |

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--kind` `TEXT` | `tool_result` | Read it as user_text, tool_result, attachment or system. |
| `--project` `PATH` |  | For the project in this folder (your own settings for it). |

approval like any change that lowers protection. With `--project`, into your own settings for the

## `latet server`

Latet on a server: one Latet for the computers and programs of a team or a company.

Its options go before the name of one of its commands: `latet server [OPTIONS] COMMAND`.

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--server` `TEXT` |  | The server's address (default: LATET_SERVER_URL, or this computer's). |
| `--fingerprint` `TEXT` |  | Its self-signed certificate's fingerprint (default: LATET_SERVER_FINGERPRINT). |
| `--admin-token-file` `PATH` |  | A file holding an administration token (or the token in LATET_SERVER_ADMIN_TOKEN, bound to LATET_SERVER_URL). |

## `latet server init`

Prepare a Latet server: its master key, the database's tables, and the first administration token.

Run it once, on a machine with the server's settings and its database's access. The master key is written to the
file master_key_file names when it is not there (in a folder that is yours alone); when nothing names one, a new key
is printed for you to keep. A token issues tokens that end no later than itself: `--never` here is how a token that
does not expire is made.

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--config` `PATH` |  | The server's settings file (server.yaml); its LATET_SERVER_* variables win over it. |
| `--new-admin-token` | off | Issue another administration token, when yours is lost. |
| `--days` `INT RANGE` |  | The token issued lasts this many days (default: admin_token_days). |
| `--never` | off | The token issued never expires: keep it apart, used only to issue others. |

## `latet server migrate`

Bring the database's tables to this version of Latet (one machine at a time: the others wait for it).

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--config` `PATH` |  | The server's settings file (server.yaml); its LATET_SERVER_* variables win over it. |
| `--check` | off | Only say whether the tables are this version's. |

## `latet server run`

Run an instance of the Latet server in the foreground: the container's command, and the services'.

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--config` `PATH` |  | The server's settings file (server.yaml); its LATET_SERVER_* variables win over it. |

## `latet server ready`

Whether this machine's instance answers ready (PostgreSQL and Valkey answer it): exit 0, else 1.

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--config` `PATH` |  | The server's settings file (server.yaml); its LATET_SERVER_* variables win over it. |

## `latet server certificate`

Show a certificate's fingerprint and expiry, or make a self-signed one for a first try.

`--make --url https://latet.acme.lan --out certs` makes certs/server.crt and certs/server.key; a file shows that
certificate; `--url` alone shows the one this computer sees at that address (a machine in between can change it:
read the fingerprint people pin from the certificate's file on the server's machine). People connect with
`latet connect <address> --fingerprint <its fingerprint>`, which asks for their one-time code.
A certificate that is an authority is no server's own, and is refused: computers given it would trust whatever its
key signs.

| Argument | | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `FILE` | optional | A certificate (PEM) to show. |

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--make` | off | Make a self-signed certificate, for a first try. |
| `--url` `TEXT` |  | The server's address: what `--make` names; alone, the certificate it shows. |
| `--out` `PATH` |  | With `--make`: the folder for server.crt and server.key. |
| `--days` `INT RANGE` | `825` | With `--make`: how long it lasts, in days. |

| --- | --- | --- |
| `--config` `PATH` |  | The server's settings file (server.yaml); its LATET_SERVER_* variables win over it. |
| `--yes` | off | Install without a prompt when run by your own script. |
| `--print` | off | Show the service plan without changing anything. |

## `latet server keys add-token`

Give an API key another token with the permissions you choose, shown once or written privately with `--out`.

A token added so calls the applications API alone, where each unmask is in the administration log: it has no
address for models, whatever it may do, and agents use the key's first token. `--forget` is given by name alone: the
key's first token cannot forget. Each token stops on its own: `keys tokens` lists them, `keys tokens --revoke`
stops one.

| Argument | | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `KEY` | required | The API key: its id or name. |
| `NAME` | required | What the token is for, such as logs. |

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--scan` | off | It may say what a text holds, and change nothing. |
| `--mask` | off | It may replace what a text holds with fakes (and so scan it). |
| `--unmask` | off | It may put the real values back in place of the fakes. |
| `--forget` | off | It may take values out of the key's vault; no other permission brings it. |
| `--out` `PATH` |  | Write the token privately; print no secret. |

## `latet server keys rotate`

Rotate one of an API key's tokens: its old secret and addresses stop on every instance within seconds.

The token keeps its name and its permissions. A key with several tokens needs `--token`; a key with one rotates
that one, which this command names to the server after listing it.

| Argument | | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `KEY` | required | The API key: its id or name. |

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--token` `TEXT` |  | The token to rotate: its id, as `keys tokens` lists it. A key with several needs it. |
| `--yes`, `-y` | off | Confirm in a script; your own terminal still asks. |
| `--out` `PATH` |  | Write the new key privately; print no secret. |

## `latet server keys limit`

Set how many values an API key's vault may hold, or give it the server's limit again.

A key with no limit of its own has the server's (vault_limit). A vault that holds the most it may refuses the
call that would add a value (the applications API answers 507) and lets nothing of that call out. A limit below
the values the vault holds is kept, and the vault takes no new value until the limit is raised or values are
forgotten (`keys forget`). The change reaches every instance within seconds.

| Argument | | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `KEY` | required | The API key: its id or name. |
| `LIMIT` | required | How many values its vault may hold (1000 to 100000000), or default for the server's limit. |

## `latet server keys forget`

Forget values of an API key's vault: each taken out of it on every instance within seconds, once you agree.

The values are read one a line from `--file`, or typed in your terminal, never from the command line. Each is found
exactly as written: another case or another written form is another value of the vault. A value forgotten is gone
with its fake, which restores nothing from then on, and it gets a new fake if it is met again. An address at a
company's domain keeps the domain as a value of its own: forget it too if it should go. Each call is recorded in
the administration log (key.forgotten) with its counts, never a value. A key's first forget after an upgrade can
take minutes on a key with much history: each call waits up to five minutes, and running it again is safe.

| Argument | | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `KEY` | required | The API key: its id or name. |

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--file` `PATH` |  | The values to forget, one a line (UTF-8); without it, type them in your terminal. |
| `--yes`, `-y` | off | Confirm in a script; your own terminal still asks. |

## `latet server keys disable`

Disable an API key: its addresses stop on every instance within seconds; its space is kept.

| Argument | | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `KEY` | required | The API key: its id or name. |

| --- | --- | --- |
| `NAME` | required | The recognizer's name. |

## `latet server rules import`

Add a rules file to an API key's settings: what adds protection; with `--all`, what lowers it too.

| Argument | | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `FILE` | required | A rules file (`latet rules export`), or a config.yaml or latet.yaml. |

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--all` | off | Also what lowers protection. |
| `--dry-run` | off | Only say what it would do. |

## `latet server rules export`

Write an API key's rules to a file (`--key`; the terms are values in clear), to share them by hand (`latet rules
import`, or Import in the dashboard).

| Argument | | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `FILE` | optional | Where to write them (none: here). |

## `latet server admin-token issue`

Issue an administration token once; `--out` keeps its secret out of a script's log.

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--label` `TEXT` |  | Whose or what it is for; required with `--never`. |
| `--days` `INT RANGE` |  | Days it lasts; default: server's admin_token_days. |
| `--never` | off | Never expires; can do all an administrator can until revoked. Only a lasting token can issue one. Keep it apart to issue others. Give CI a token with `--days`. |
| `--out` `PATH` |  | Write a private {url, token} record; print no secret. |

## `latet server admin-token list`

Every token: this marks the one in use; tampered rows open nothing; never a secret.

## `latet server admin-token revoke`

Revoke a token; revoking this or the last one asks and explains the way back.

| Argument | | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TOKEN_ID` | required | The administration token id, never its secret. |

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--yes`, `-y` | off | Confirm in a script; your own terminal still asks. |

## `latet server log`

The administration log: who did what, when, on what, from where (never a value); `verify` checks its chain.

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--since` `TEXT` |  | From: 7d, 12h, or an ISO date. |
| `--until` `TEXT` |  | Until: excluded; accepts exact epoch seconds too. |
| `--action` `TEXT` |  | One action. |
| `--actor` `TEXT` |  | An identity id or admin:<token id>. |
| `--cursor` `TEXT` |  | Resume cursor, with the same original filters. |
| `--limit` `INT RANGE` | `100` | Maximum entries to read. |
| `--json` | off | JSON lines, with exact id and ts. |

## `latet server log verify`

Walk the log's chain and print its head for a copy kept elsewhere.
